providers.name: Crypto Emporium
providers.howToPay: Named processor — on-site checkout, property priced directly in BTC with a 'Buy now' button; storefront settles the order
providers.quote: lets you buy a property with Bitcoin, Ethereum and other major cryptocurrencies
providers.shipsTo: No. Properties are location-fixed and none observed in Canada — listings seen were Greece, Spain, UK, Italy, Portugal, France, Germany, Mexico, USA, Argentina. An Alberta buyer is buying abroad.
providers.priceFrom: ~4.44 BTC (cheapest property observed; cheapest IN-STOCK was 4.854782 BTC, Caldas da Rainha, Portugal)
providers.caveat: CORRECTION TO SEED: the header coin strip shows BTC/LTC/ETH/DOGE/XRP/DASH/USDT — I did NOT verify SOL or USDC. Filters are Apartment/House/Investment/Land: there is no prefab, modular, tiny-home or eco category, so this is existing-stock real estate, not an eco-home provider. A large share of listings show 'Out of stock'. I did not reach a live escrow/terms page (both URLs 404), so the seed's escrow-until-close claim is UNVERIFIED in this sweep.

providers.name: RAK Properties PJSC
providers.productType: developer unit (waterfront apartments, Mina Al Arab / Mina district)
providers.howToPay: Named processor — Hubpay (ADGM-licensed) converts crypto to AED instantly and settles fiat to the developer; RAK never touches the digital asset
providers.quote: Clients can now pay for property using major digital assets like USDT, BTC, ETH
providers.shipsTo: No — UAE-situated property only. A Canadian buyer must transact in the UAE and clear Hubpay/VARA onboarding; nothing is delivered to Alberta.
providers.caveat: Cleanest regulated model found and the only entry where the crypto rail is explicitly a licensed processor — but the developer makes NO eco or sustainability claim anywhere in the announcement, so calling it an 'eco home' would be unsupported. Announcement dated Sept 1, 2025; the crypto rail is described as newly enabled, not as a track record.

providers.name: Armstrong Steel
providers.productType: kit — pre-engineered steel building systems, incl. residential steel homes and barndominiums
providers.howToPay: Unstated. The acceptance page describes no wallet, processor, or conversion mechanism — a buyer would have to negotiate it on a quote call
providers.quote: Bitcoin and Dogecoin are the two cryptocurrencies that Armstrong Steel is currently accepting
providers.shipsTo: Unverified. US manufacturer; no Canadian delivery statement found on the site. Treat cross-border shipping, duty and CSA/Alberta code compliance as an open question.
providers.caveat: THE DATE IS THE STORY: that acceptance page is dated February 20, 2014 — twelve years stale. I fetched the current homepage and it names NO payment methods at all; 'Residential — steel homes, barndominiums' is a live category, but crypto appears nowhere on it. Separately, third-party review sites carry a 1.0/5 rating with repeated reports of non-delivery after deposit. Do not route a judge or a buyer here without saying both things out loud.

providers.name: Robinson Home Builders
providers.productType: custom homes, additions and ADUs (site-built, not prefab)
providers.howToPay: Direct wallet transfer — seven receiving addresses published on-page, plus a form where you submit your sending address for manual verification
providers.quote: one of the first construction companies to accept cryptocurrency payments
providers.shipsTo: No — a local Massachusetts build radius. Irrelevant to an Alberta buyer except as proof the model exists.
providers.priceFrom: not published for construction; the only priced item on the page is a $45 hoodie
providers.caveat: MATERIAL DOWNGRADE FROM SEED. The wallet addresses are real and the seven chains check out, but the ONLY thing with a working payment path on that page is $45 branded merchandise. The construction copy ('full home builds to minor renovations') is aspirational: no deposit schedule, no milestone draws, no minimum, no escrow, no conversion policy — nothing a buyer could actually execute. Paying six figures to a raw address with no escrow is also the single riskiest pattern in this whole directory.

providers.name: BOXABL
providers.productType: modular — foldable factory-built housing units (Casita and successors)
assets: unspecified — the release says 'cryptocurrencies' and names none
providers.howToPay: Unstated. No wallet, processor, or checkout path disclosed anywhere I could verify
providers.quote: BOXABL accepts cryptocurrencies as payment for the sale of its innovative housing products
providers.shipsTo: Unverified. US factory shipping foldable units by road; no Canadian delivery, duty or code-compliance statement found.
providers.priceFrom: not published (the crypto release names no price)
providers.caveat: The sentence is BOXABL's own words, but it appears buried in a BITCOIN TREASURY press release (May 22, 2025) — the release is about buying BTC for the balance sheet, and the acceptance line is a single passing clause. Seed's caveat still holds after re-check: the company's own FAQ never mentions crypto, no coin is named, and no mechanics exist. This is the weakest 'yes' in the list; closest in spirit to what Aura wants, furthest from being executable.

providers.name: Lib Work Co., Ltd. (TSE: 1431)
providers.productType: 3D-printed earth home — 'Lib Earth House model B', natural materials + 3D printing
providers.howToPay: Not yet operational — announced as a future settlement option alongside issuing the design data as an NFT
providers.shipsTo: No — Japanese domestic housing product. Not available to a Canadian buyer.
providers.caveat: DOWNGRADE: this is a 販売構想 — a sales CONCEPT — not a live payment rail. The company's own release says orders begin January 2026 and adds that its crypto holding policy 'remains undecided at this time.' I fetched libwork.co.jp and found ZERO mentions of bitcoin, 暗号資産 or NFT on the homepage. So as of this sweep there is no evidence the January 2026 launch actually shipped. Still the closest thing worldwide to an eco/3D-printed home maker taking BTC — but it is an announcement, and must be labelled as one.

providers.name: Hotomobil (CyberGlad)
providers.productType: unique-stay pod — insulated four-season camper cabin that drops into a Tesla Cybertruck bed
providers.howToPay: Reservation/build-slot deposit taken in Bitcoin at launch; the company's own release names no processor (secondary press claims BitPay — unverified)
providers.quote: the first camper offered for sale in Bitcoin
providers.shipsTo: Unverified. Release says Hotomobil is 'expanding into North and South America' but names no Canadian channel. Alberta delivery is an open question.
providers.priceFrom: not published in the company release; press coverage cites US$24,000 (Body) to US$66,600 (Exclusive)
providers.caveat: Two honest catches. First, it is NOT a home — it is a truck-bed camper cabin, relevant only to the unique-stays rental angle, and it needs a Cybertruck. Second, I fetched cyberglad.hotomobil.com directly and found no bitcoin or crypto mention in the live site's visible content — the BTC offer exists only in the May 30, 2025 launch release from the Bitcoin 2025 conference. The BitPay detail comes from secondary press, not the company, so do not repeat it as fact.

refuted: Miradex.ro (Romania — prefab timber-frame nZEB/Passive House kits): THE MOST IMPORTANT NEGATIVE. Cryptwerk lists it under construction companies accepting crypto, and it is a genuine eco-prefab maker (since 1992, 300+ projects, timber-frame house kits) — exactly the profile Aura wants. But its own site has zero crypto payment content. A regex on miradex.ro returned 16 apparent 'cripto' hits that are ALL inside the word 'des-cripto-r' in Wix JavaScript. Refuted.
High Performance Homes (Vancouver, WA): listed on the Cryptwerk construction directory; own site returned 0 visible crypto mentions. Also roofing/siding/windows, not homes. Refuted.

Energize Builders (Los Angeles): seed carried a B-press claim of '200+ crypto-funded projects'. Fetched energizebuilders.com — 0 visible crypto mentions on the live site. Refuted pending better evidence.

Trademark Renovations (Calgary, ALBERTA): the single most locally relevant lead in the whole sweep. CBC and the Globe and Mail reported in 2018 that it was the first Canadian general contractor to accept bitcoin and ether, and it does build custom homes. Its live site today mentions bitcoin, ethereum and cryptocurrency NOWHERE. Refuted — an eight-year-old headline, not a current rail.

cryptorealestate.com ('Crypto Real Estate'): Cryptwerk describes it as the largest global crypto real-estate marketplace with 1500+ listings. The live site is an unfinished GoDaddy template — 'Launching Soon' placeholders and stock filler copy ('Generate excitement', 'Say something interesting about your business here'). Refuted.

Naples Luxury Builders (Florida): seed listed it A-own-site for BTC. Could not confirm — naplesluxurybuilders.com returned an effectively empty body and the seed-adjacent domain napleluxurybuilders.com does not resolve. Unverifiable in this sweep; do not publish as a provider.
ADU Start (Canada): surfaces high in searches for Canadian crypto real estate, but it is an informational directory, not a builder, and accepts no crypto itself. Refuted.

Bookaglamping.com: DOES accept crypto (BTC, ETH, SOL, LTC, DOGE, XRP, BCH, USDC via BitPay) — but it sells glamping STAYS, not structures. Not a home provider; listed here so nobody re-checks it as one. Relevant only to the unique-stays rental use case as a demand-side comparable.

Cryptwerk 'Construction' directory as a source: 26 merchants listed, but every housing-relevant entry I spot-checked (Miradex, High Performance Homes) failed own-site verification, and the rest are trades — plumbing, roofing, fencing, painting, architecture. Treat the whole directory as C-tier lead generation only; never cite it as evidence of acceptance.

Baltic/Scandinavian prefab (Nordland House, Modhouse, Dolena, SPARS AP, VIA-S, Bitus): searched specifically because the jurisdictions are crypto-forward. No crypto payment claim found for any prefab manufacturer in Estonia, Latvia or Lithuania. Nothing to verify.

Container-home makers (Backcountry Containers, ROXBOX, Amish Built Cabins, Sweet-Haus, Glitzcamp): searched the container and tiny-home angle. The only container/crypto overlap is companies selling containers FOR bitcoin mining, not residential container homes sold FOR bitcoin. Refuted.

A-frame and kit-cabin sellers (Avrame, Den, 7 Day A-Frames, DC Structures, Backcountry Hut Co., Lushna): searched the A-frame/kit-cabin and glamping-pod angle explicitly. No crypto acceptance found for any of them.

NOT RE-VERIFIED IN THIS SWEEP — do not publish these as providers without a live fetch: Gafisa (Brazil, B-press via Foxbit), DAMAC (Dubai, B-press), and Wallaya Villas (Phuket, seed already had a 403). I ran out of sweep on these three; they carry over as open, not as confirmed.
